bandReport.notes: Contiguous Q48-Q100, no gaps. SEAM: opened p07 (band b1's territory, printed p17) — it holds Q42-Q47 and Q47 ends complete with all four options on that page, so nothing straddles into p08 and my Q48 opens clean at the top of the left column. There is no page after p15 (the render is 16 pages). PAPER ENDS AT Q100: p15 (printed p33) carries Q97-Q100 and the lower ~55% of the page is blank — the paper genuinely terminates there. NO DIRECTIONS SETS ANYWHERE IN MY BAND: unlike the sibling papers, every one of these 53 questions is standalone with no shared stimulus — no data-interpretation table, no data-sufficiency block, no shared-passage set. So no question carries context/setLabel. NO FIGURES in p08-p15; every geometry item (Q48, Q55, Q65, Q69, Q70) states its configuration entirely in words, so no hasFigure/figureNote anywhere. NO ANSWER KEY on any page of my band. Q72 and Q80 are multi-statement items whose statement list sits at the foot of the left column with the 'Which of the above...' line and options at the head of the right column; both are complete on their own page (p11 and p12) and are transcribed whole. Q79's stem is likewise split across the column break on p12 and is complete. CURRENCY: Q74, Q83 print the rupee glyph; rendered as 'Rs.' per the corpus convention (Rs. is used across every sibling band; no band uses the glyph). STRUCTURAL, this being the oldest sitting attempted: printed page numbers on my band run 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33 — odd only, i.e. the render carries just the English pages of a bilingual booklet, and the booklet series code is 'C - SDHY-T-MTH' in every footer. Layout is otherwise the familiar two-column, 6-8 questions per page (7,7,7,7,6,7,8,4). Decimals print as a raised middle dot throughout (0.301, 3.0212, 4.75, 4.232323...) and are transcribed as full stops per the brief; each was read at zoom to confirm it is a decimal point and not multiplication. AMBIGUOUS GLYPHS CHECKED AT 3x ZOOM: Q52 'radius 201 mm' (confirmed 201, an unusual value but the radius cancels out of the ratio asked), Q56 option signs, Q58 exponents 0.3475/0.3375/0.3275/0.3735, Q59 all four expansions, Q65 EB=25/FC=16, Q67 volume 155232, Q70 options 3744 vs 3777, Q71 fraction 26/5, Q77 exponents 7^25/8^23/9^20, Q80 statements 2-4, Q82 continued fraction nesting, Q86 6^23 x 75^9 x 105^2, Q87 3^98 - 3^89, Q92 nested radical, Q93 denominator, Q96 n^2+19n+92, Q99 set contents, Q100 px^2+3x+2q. MISPRINTS: none found — no defective option sets, no self-contradictory data, no duplicated options. Two presentational notes flagged on their questions rather than treated as errors: Q95 prints 'not' in italics for emphasis, and Q99's stem ends 'equals to' with no question mark. SUBTOPICS: none invented; every chapter and subtopic is a catalog key. Two multi-topic items carry a flag explaining the filing rather than forcing a bad fit — Q80 (statements 1 and 4 are Number System, 2 and 3 are Inequalities) and Q95 (mixes prime/composite, sign, parity and irrationality). Q57 asks which quantities' logarithms are needed to find a triangle's area; the underlying skill is Heron's formula, so it is filed under Mensuration 2D rather than Logarithms. A stray diagonal pen/scan mark crosses the left edge of Q100 on p15; it obscures nothing.

questions.stem: \(ABC\) is a triangle right angled at \(B\). If \(AB = 5\) cm and \(BC = 10\) cm, then what is the length of the perpendicular drawn from the vertex \(B\) to the hypotenuse ?

questions.stem: Two cylinders of equal volume have their heights in the ratio \(2 : 3\). What is the ratio of their radii ?
The length and breadth of a rectangle are increased by 20% and 10% respectively. What is the percentage increase in the area of the rectangle ?
If the length of the hypotenuse of a right angled triangle is 10 cm, then what is the maximum area of such a right angled triangle ?
A square is drawn such that its vertices are lying on a circle of radius 201 mm. What is the ratio of area of circle to that of square ?
A right circular cylinder has a diameter of 20 cm and its curved surface area is 1000 \(\text{cm}^2\). What is the volume of the cylinder ?
A piece of wire of length 33 cm is bent into an arc of a circle of radius 14 cm. What is the angle subtended by the arc at the centre of the circle ?
What is the ratio of the area of a square inscribed in a semicircle of radius \(r\) to the area of square inscribed in a circle of radius \(r\) ?
The quotient when \(x^4 - x^2 + 7x + 5\) is divided by \((x + 2)\) is \(ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d\). What are the values of \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) and \(d\) respectively ?
The sides of a triangle are 30 cm, 28 cm and 16 cm respectively. In order to determine its area, the logarithm of which of the quantities are required ?

questions.stem: What is \((x - a)(x - b)(x - c)\) equal to ?

Let \(XYZ\) be an equilateral triangle in which \(XY = 7\) cm. If \(A\) denotes the area of the triangle, then what is the value of \(\log_{10} A^4\) ? (Given that \(\log_{10} 1050 = 3.0212\) and \(\log_{10} 35 = 1.5441\))
questions.subtopic: Logarithm Identities and Change of Base

questions.stem: A hollow sphere of external and internal diameters 6 cm and 4 cm respectively is melted into a cone of base diameter 8 cm. What is the height of the cone ?

A solid metallic cylinder of height 10 cm and radius 6 cm is melted to make two cones in the ratio of volume \(1 : 2\) and of same height as 10 cm. What is the percentage increase in the flat surface area ?
If one side of a right-angled triangle (with all sides integers) is 15 cm, then what is the maximum perimeter of the triangle ?
A thin rod of length 24 feet is cut into rods of equal size and joined so as to form a skeleton cube. What is the area of one of the faces of the largest cube thus constructed ?

Consider a trapezium \(ABCD\), in which \(AB\) is parallel to \(CD\) and \(AD\) is perpendicular to \(AB\). If the trapezium has an incircle which touches \(AB\) at \(E\) and \(CD\) at \(F\), where \(EB = 25\) cm and \(FC = 16\) cm, then what is the diameter of the circle ?
Three copper spheres of radii 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm are melted to form a large sphere. What is its radius ?
The volume of a hemisphere is 155232 \(\text{cm}^3\). What is the radius of the hemisphere ?
A bucket is in the form of a truncated cone. The diameters of the base and top of the bucket are 6 cm and 12 cm respectively. If the height of the bucket is 7 cm, what is the capacity of the bucket ?
A right circular cone has height 8 cm. If the radius of its base is 6 cm, then what is its total surface area ?
Six cubes, each with 12 cm edge are joined end to end. What is the surface area of resulting cuboid ?
If the sum of a real number and its reciprocal is \(\frac{26}{5}\), then how many such numbers are possible ?

Consider the following statements :

1. If \(p\) is relatively prime to each of \(q\) and \(r\), then \(p\) is relatively prime to the product \(qr\).

2. If \(p\) divides the product \(qr\) and if \(p\) divides \(q\), then \(p\) must divide \(r\).

Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
Radha and Rani are sisters. Five years back, the age of Radha was three times that of Rani, but one year back the age of Radha was two times that of Rani. What is the age difference between them ?

A person carries Rs. 500 and wants to buy apples and oranges out of it. If the cost of one apple is Rs. 5 and the cost of one orange is Rs. 7, then what is the number of ways in which a person can buy both apples and oranges using total amount ?
Given \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{x}\), and \(x = 36\) when \(y = 36\). What is the value of \(x\) when \(y = 54\) ?
What is the square root of \(16 + 6\sqrt{7}\) ?
Let \(x\) be the smallest positive integer such that when 14 divides \(x\), the remainder is 7; and when 15 divides \(x\), the remainder is 5. Which one of the following is correct ?

Two taps \(X\) and \(Y\) are fixed to a water tank. If only \(X\) is opened, it drains out the full tank of water in 20 minutes. If both \(X\) and \(Y\) are opened, then they drain out the full tank of water in 15 minutes. If only \(Y\) is opened, how long does it take to drain out the full tank of water ?

Consider the following statements :

1. \(\sqrt{75}\) is a rational number.

2. There exists at least a positive integer \(x\) such that \(-\frac{4x}{5} < -\frac{7}{8}\).

3. \(\frac{x-2}{x} < 1\) for all real values of \(x\).

4. \(4.232323......\) can be expressed in the form \(\frac{p}{q}\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are integers.

Which of the above statements are correct ?
flags: Multi-statement item spanning two chapters: statements 1 and 4 are Number System (rational/irrational), statements 2 and 3 are Inequalities. Filed under the majority chapter.
